neighbours.label: narration of people injured, dying or trapped in a disaster or emergency scene
fire: After the explosion, injured workers were crawling out of the collapsed warehouse, coughing and bleeding.
Rescuers found the climber lying motionless in the snow, his hands frozen and blue.
Within minutes the corridor was filling with black smoke, and patients were screaming for help.
Burned and wounded passengers were pulled from the wreckage of the derailed train.
Many of the refugees were clearly starving, their ribs showing beneath torn shirts.
The flood had trapped dozens of families on rooftops, where some had been waiting for two days without water.
A firefighter carried the unconscious girl down the ladder as the roof began to give way.
Bodies of the drowned sailors washed up on the beach for nearly a week after the storm.
quiet: After the inspection, the workers were walking out of the renovated warehouse, chatting and laughing.
Rescuers found the climber sitting comfortably in the hut, his hands wrapped around a hot mug.
Within minutes the corridor was filling with visitors, and patients were chatting with their families.
Cheerful passengers were stepping off the newly opened train at the decorated station.
Many of the volunteers were clearly hungry after the long shift, so we ordered pizza.
The festival had brought dozens of families onto the rooftops, where some had been watching fireworks for hours.
A firefighter carried the smiling girl down the ladder during the station's open day.
Crates of fresh fish arrived on the beach for nearly a week after the boats came home.

notes: Card: top examples are function words inside descriptions of casualties (lifeless on the pavement, wounded and burned men, control room filling with smoke, starvation, emergency patients). Output promotes 'as/increasingly/aware'.
